newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs close lower on trade woes, ignore Dow.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs close lower on trade woes, ignore Dow.

text.p: Despite higher Wall Street stock prices, Brazilian shares ended lower as investors were still digesting the impact of Tuesday's government measures limiting imports on the country's trade balance, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most active stocks closed off 1.16 percent at 9,272 points.
Market turnover was lower than usual at 431.4 million reais ($406.9 million) ahead of the Easter break.
"We still don't know how the measures will help reduce the trade gap," said a senior trader.
Late Tuesday, Brazil's Central Bank announced new rules to limit the attractiveness of short-term import financing.
Most importers with financing of less than 360 days will have to take out foreign exchange contracts on the day they retrieve their goods from customs.
Brazil has been facing a widening trade deficit, which in the first three weeks of March has amounted to $819 million.
Analysts also said nervousness over the fate of ailing local private bank Bamerindus contributed to the depression of prices.
The Sao Paulo Stock Exchange (Bovespa) halted trade in Bamerindus stock ten minutes before the market's close, a bourse spokeswoman said.
After the end of the session, the Central Bank announced it intervened in the bank, which has been facing serious liquidity troubles.

The Central Bank's intervention puts an end to months of speculation that the bank would be sold at any moment or that it would be managed by independent consultants in a prior step to its sale. reais, while its common stock lost 1.35 percent to end at 109.50 reais.

State mining giant Vale do Rio Doce closed at 24.80 reais, down 1.0 percent. Brazilian bourses will be closed Thursday and Friday for Easter holidays. ((--Fatima Cristina, Sao Paulo Newsroom 5511 2485412))
